The '''2023 Copa Sudamericana final''' was the final match which decided the winner of the [[2023 Copa Sudamericana]]. This was the 22nd edition of the [[Copa Sudamericana]], the second-tier South American continental club [[Association football|football]] tournament organized by [[CONMEBOL]].

The match was played on 28 October 2023 between Brazilian club [[Fortaleza Esporte Clube|Fortaleza]] and Ecuadorian club [[L.D.U. Quito|LDU Quito]], and it was originally scheduled to be played at [[Estadio Centenario]] in [[Montevideo]], Uruguay,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.elobservador.com.uy/nota/conmebol-confirmo-la-fecha-y-donde-se-jugara-la-final-de-la-copa-libertadores-2023-202342593629 |title=Conmebol confirmó la fecha y dónde se jugará la final de la Copa Libertadores |trans-title=CONMEBOL confirmed the date and where the Copa Libertadores final will be played |publisher=[[El Observador (Uruguay)|El Observador]] |language=es |date=25 April 2023 |access-date=24 May 2023}}</ref> but on 15 September 2023, [[Estadio Domingo Burgueño]] in Maldonado was confirmed as the venue for the final.<ref name=Relocation>{{cite web |url=https://www.montevideo.com.uy/Deportes/Sudamericana-la-final-se-disputara-en-el-Campus-de-Maldonado-por-pedido-de-Brasil-uc865562|title=Sudamericana: la final se disputará en el Campus de Maldonado por pedido de Brasil|trans-title=Sudamericana: The final will be played at the Maldonado Campus at the request of Brazil |publisher=Montevideo Portal|language=es |date=15 September 2023|access-date=15 September 2023}}</ref>

LDU Quito were the champions, winning their second title in the competition after defeating Fortaleza 4–3 on [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalties]] following a 1–1 draw [[Overtime (sports)#Association football|after extra time]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://conmebolsudamericana.com/cards/NewsReaderWeb/liga-de-quito-campeon-de-la-conmebol-sudamericana |title=Liga de Quito, campeón de la CONMEBOL Sudamericana |trans-title=Liga de Quito, champion of the CONMEBOL Sudamericana |publisher=CONMEBOL Sudamericana |language=es |date=28 October 2023 |access-date=28 October 2023}}</ref> As winners of the 2023 Copa Sudamericana, LDU Quito earned the right to play against the winners of the [[2023 Copa Libertadores]] in the [[2024 Recopa Sudamericana]]. They also automatically qualified for the [[2024 Copa Libertadores]] group stage.

==Venue==
===Original host selection===
Although in January 2023 CONMEBOL president [[Alejandro Domínguez (football executive)|Alejandro Domínguez]] had expressed an intention to hold the final match at [[Estádio Nacional Mané Garrincha]] in [[Brasília]] in compensation for the [[2022 Copa Sudamericana final|2022 final]] that could not be played at that stadium as originally planned due to the [[2022 Brazilian general election]],<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com.br/futebol/sul-americana/artigo/_/id/11460408/presidente-conmebol-final-sul-americana-brasilia-maos-cbf |title=Presidente da Conmebol, Alejandro Domínguez quer final da Sul-Americana em Brasília: 'Está nas mãos da CBF' |trans-title=CONMEBOL president Alejandro Domínguez wants Sudamericana final in Brasília: "It's in the CBF's hands" |publisher=[[ESPN (Brazil)|ESPN]] |language=pt-br |date=10 January 2023 |access-date=20 May 2024}}</ref> [[Estadio Centenario]] in [[Montevideo]], Uruguay was selected as the host for the 2023 final by CONMEBOL during their meeting on 25 April 2023. The stadium had previously hosted the 2021 finals of both the [[2021 Copa Libertadores final|Copa Libertadores]] and [[2021 Copa Sudamericana final|Copa Sudamericana]], with the latter sparking criticism due to the poor attendance as less than a third of the stadium's capacity was filled by the fans.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.futbolred.com/copa-sudamericana/2021-poco-publico-en-montevideo-para-paranaense-vs-bragantino-148443 |title=Ridículo internacional de Conmebol en la final de Copa Suramericana |trans-title=CONMEBOL's international ridicule in the Copa Sudamericana final |publisher=Futbolred |language=es |date=21 November 2021 |access-date=20 May 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.eluniverso.com/deportes/futbol/copa-libertadores-conmebol-asume-el-fracaso-de-las-finales-unicas-y-planea-un-cambio-radical-dice-el-diario-as-nota/ |title=Copa Libertadores: 'Conmebol asume el fracaso de las finales únicas y planea un cambio radical', dice el diario AS |trans-title=Copa Libertadores: 'CONMEBOL assumes the failure of single-match finals and plans a radical change,' says the newspaper AS |publisher=[[El Universo]] |language=es |date=26 October 2022 |access-date=20 May 2024}}</ref>

===Relocation to Maldonado===
On 15 September 2023, the CONMEBOL president announced a relocation of the final to the [[Estadio Domingo Burgueño]] in [[Maldonado, Uruguay]].<ref name=Relocation/> A request from the [[Brazilian Football Confederation]] (CBF) to not hold the match in Montevideo on safety grounds as well as an attempt to avoid the low attendance levels of previous finals were considered to be the reasons behind the move.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.encancha.cl/internacional/copa-sudamericana/2023/09/15/quieren-evitar-otro-papelon-la-conmebol-programa-la-final-de-la-copa-sudamericana-en-un-mini-estadio/ |title=Quieren evitar otro papelón: la Conmebol programa la final de la Copa Sudamericana en un mini estadio |trans-title=They want to avoid another faux pas: CONMEBOL schedules the final of the Copa Sudamericana at a mini stadium |publisher=En Cancha |language=es |date=21 November 2021 |access-date=20 May 2024}}</ref>
